p2: name split into 'Phulana' with 'nāyaka' moved to titles (headman title), confidence lowered to medium; residence corrected to Yupaṭola(ka) per 'yupaṭolakādhivāsino'.

purpose: dharmārtha (for merit), for the owner Phulana(nāyaka)
notes: The year 'ā 7' uses letter-numerals. I follow the cataloguer's NS 207 (= 1087 CE). I have not verified this independently. Era 'samvat' is unspecified but the letter-numerals point to NS. The place of copying is not stated. Yupaṭolaka is where the owner lives, and Pannugaviṣaya is the district governed by the mahāsāmanta. Identifying Pannugaviṣaya with Panauti is possible but unproven. 'nāyaka' in Phulananāyaka may be part of the name and not a title. It is not stated that he commissioned the copy, but this is implied ('his book, written for merit'). The catalogue calls him donor, but the colophon has no donation formula. Raphasadīva/Raphasadeva is a mahāsāmanta, a feudatory ruler of a district, not a king: 'vijayarāje' marks his rule. The names Tejādīta and Raphasadīva are likely misspellings of -āditya and -deva. The colophon ending names Kubjikāmata (dvādaśasāhasrikā), chapter 32 'tripurāyoga', which does not match the catalogue title Uttaraṣaṭkaṭīkā.
